zone.title: Am I in an evacuation zone?
zone.naturalWarningSource: Source: National Weather Service tsunami safety guidance

safety.naturalWarning: If you feel a strong earthquake or see the ocean suddenly pull back, move inland or to high ground right away. Do not wait for an official warning.
safety.tsunamiZoneAction: If a Tsunami Warning is issued, or you feel a strong earthquake, leave this zone right away. Go inland or uphill, on foot if you can. Do not go to the shore to watch.
safety.extremeZoneAction: Leave this area if officials issue an Extreme Tsunami Warning. For any other tsunami warning, follow official instructions.
safety.safeZoneAction: During a tsunami warning, stay where you are unless officials tell you to move. Keep roads clear for people who are evacuating.
safety.tsunamiGoUp: Getting out of the zone matters more than reaching a shelter. If you cannot get out in time, go to an upper floor of a tall, sturdy concrete building.
safety.refugeNotOpen: These are possible hurricane refuge areas, not open shelters. Officials announce which ones open, and when, on radio, TV and official social media. They are a last resort and have no supplies: bring your emergency kit, food, water and medicine.
safety.tsunamiAlertAction: A tsunami alert is active. If you are in a tsunami evacuation zone and officials say to evacuate, go inland or uphill now. Stay away from the shore until officials say it is safe.

plan.intro: Fill this in with your household now, while things are calm. It stays on this phone only, and works offline.
plan.membersHint: Names, ages, and anything responders should know: medical needs, mobility, pets.
plan.homeLocation: Home location for the zone check
plan.homeHowTo: To set it, use your location or tap your home on the Zone map, then come back here.
plan.useCheckedSpot: Use the spot I last checked
plan.meetingNearHint: For example, the mailbox or a neighbor’s driveway. Used for fires.
plan.meetingAway: Meeting place away from the neighborhood
plan.meetingAwayHint: Somewhere outside the tsunami zone, like a relative’s house or a school on high ground.
plan.outOfAreaHint: Long-distance calls and texts often get through when local ones don’t. Everyone checks in with this person.
plan.checklistIntro: Hawaiʻi emergency agencies recommend supplies for at least 14 days, because help and shipments can take weeks to arrive after a big storm.

items.water: Water: 1 gallon per person per day, for 14 days
items.food: Food that doesn’t need cooking, for 14 days, and a can opener
items.meds: Medicines (2 weeks) and copies of prescriptions
items.charger: Phone power bank or car charger
items.ids: Copies of IDs and birth certificates
items.insurance: Insurance and bank papers, in a waterproof bag
items.medicalList: List of medical conditions, doctors and medicines
items.contactsPaper: Contact list on paper (print this plan)
items.knowZone: Know if home, work and school are in a tsunami zone
items.shutoffs: Know how to shut off water, power and gas
items.secureOutside: Plan to secure or bring in outdoor items before a storm
items.gasTank: Keep the car’s gas tank at least half full
items.kupuna: Plan for kūpuna or anyone who needs help moving
items.keiki: Plan for keiki: school pickup, comfort items
items.pets: Pet food, water, carrier, leash and records
items.neighbors: Know which neighbors might need help

plan.notesHint: Anything else: where the kit is stored, a spare key, insurance policy numbers.
plan.exportIntro: Phones die. Print a copy for the fridge and the emergency kit, or let family scan the code.
plan.qrLabel: QR code with the text of this family plan
plan.qrHelp: Scan with a phone camera to get the plan as text.
plan.privacy: This plan is saved only on this phone. Kōkua never uploads it.
plan.printFooter: Made with Kōkua. Check your tsunami zone and keep this copy with your emergency kit.

checkin.heading: Tell family you’re safe
checkin.intro: Kōkua writes the message and keeps it ready. Your phone’s texting app sends it. Texts often get through when calls and data don’t.
checkin.noContacts: Add emergency contacts below so the message goes to them.
checkin.pending: Your “I’m safe” message is ready to send:
checkin.bannerBackOnline: You’re back online and your “I’m safe” message hasn’t been sent yet.

settings.title: Settings
settings.highContrastHint: Black and white with strong outlines. Easier to read in bright sun.
settings.kupunaHint: One screen with very large buttons: check where you are, call 911, tell family you’re safe.
settings.translationsBody: Kōkua is available in these languages. Most translations were made by machine and are waiting for review by native speakers. Until a safety instruction has been reviewed, Kōkua shows it in English.
settings.aboutBody: Kōkua helps Hawaiʻi households prepare for and respond to tsunamis, hurricanes and floods, even with no internet. It uses official public data. It does not replace official warnings or instructions.
settings.privacy: No accounts, no tracking. Everything you enter stays on this phone.
